question:
What Utah regulation currently adopts the FDA Food Code 2026, and what penalties
does it impose on a restaurant that violates employee-illness rules?
message: The retrieved passages are from the FDA Food Code 2026 (a model code) and do not contain Utah regulations or penalties. Utah adoption of the FDA Food Code 2026 and associated penalties are not specified in the provided documents.

FDA Food Code 2026  Chapter 2. Management and Personnel 
44 
*CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES, the *PERSON-IN-CHARGE, and required reporting to 
the *REGULATORY AUTHORITY:  
(1) Illness symptoms of diarrhea, vomiting, sore throat with fever, jaundice or 
infected wounds or cuts; Pf 
(2) Illness disease diagnosis due to norovirus, hepatitis A virus, Shigella spp., 
Typhoid fever, non-typhoidal Salmonella, or *SHIGA TOXIN-PRODUCING 
ESCHERICHIA COLI; Pf and 
(3) Illness *EXCLUSION and/or *RESTRICTION and reinstatement after illness 
symptom or disease resolution. Pf 
2-502 Contamination Event Response Procedures 
2-502.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events 
A *FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for *EMPLOYEES to follow 
when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of 
vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the *FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The 
procedures shall address the specific actions *EMPLOYEES must take to minimize 
the spread of contamination and the exposure of *EMPLOYEES, *CONSUMERS, 
*FOOD and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Pf

FDA Food Code 2026  Summary of Changes 
Summary-645 
2-301.16  
Amended Public Health Reason for § 2-301.16 Hand Antiseptics to revise paragraphs 2 
and 3 to clarify the intent of hand antiseptics.  
2-303.11   
Amended Public Health Reasons for § 2-303.11 Prohibition, to 
address an additional exception for individuals with disabilities covered by the Americans 
with Disabilities Act, to wear a medically necessary device.  
2-5   
• Amended Public Health Reasons to add new Part 2-5 to address written policy 
and procedures requirements for employee illness   
• Amended Public Health Reasons to add new subPart 2-501 to address what 
an employee illness policy is and the purpose of an illness policy for each food 
establishment.     
• Amended Public Health Reasons for the previous § 2-501.11 to 
new title “Employee Illness Policy Documentation” to address the basic 
components of an Employee Illness Policy.  “Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal 
Events” was moved to a new § 2-502.11.  
• Amended Public Health Reasons to add new subPart 2-502; “Contamination 
Event Response Procedures” to cover all contamination event responses.     
• Amended Public Health Reasons to add new § 2-502.11 “Clean-up of Vomiting 
and Diarrheal event” to include the previous § 2-501.11 for “Procedures 
for Responding to Vomiting and Diarrheal Events.”     
• Amended Public Health Reasons for previous § 2-501.11, new § 2-502.11, 
Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events to revise paragraph 6 to include 
reference to EPA-registered disinfectants and to revise paragraph 9 by 
rearranging bulleted list of items to consider when developing a written plan to 
ensure the steps listed reflect the order of actions covered by the plan.  
3-201.11  
Amended Annex 3 Public Health Reasons for § 3-201.11 to delete the word “not” 
between “have” and “undergone” in sentence 3 under the section Labeling for Whole-
muscle, Intact Beef Steaks. This was a typographical error.  
3-204.10  
Amended Public Health Reasons for § 3-204.10 to include paragraphs 4-6 to address 
economically adulterated foods.   
3-301.11  
• Amended Public Health Reasons for § 3-301.11 to add new paragraphs 3, 4 and 
5 to introduce additional control measures, provide more background describing 
what a double handwash is and to include information on fingernail brushes from 
the Public Health Reasons found in § 2-301.12.

FDA Food Code 2026 Annex 7. Model Forms, Guides, and Other Aids 
604 
4. Proper use of restriction and exclusion. 
IN/OUT This item must be marked IN or OUT of compliance. Compliance must be based on 
firsthand observations or information and cannot be based solely on responses from the 
PIC to questions regarding hypothetical situations or knowledge of the Food Code. This 
item is marked IN when the following criteria are observed at the time of the inspection:  
• There are no ill employees.  
• There are no employees experiencing symptoms with or without a diagnosis that 
require reporting, or reason for the PIC to exclude or restrict an employee.  
• A food employee who works in a food establishment serving a HSP or non-HSP,  is 
restricted due to diagnoses with an infection from non-typhoidal Salmonella and is 
asymptomatic. 
This item should be marked OUT of compliance when: 
• The inspector observes a working employee with specific reportable symptoms under 
Sub-¶ 2-201.11(A)(1).  
• The inspector becomes aware than an employee has reported information about his 
or her health and activities as it relates to diseases that are transmissible through 
food and the PIC has not acted to restrict/exclude an employee under §§ 2-201.12 
and 2-201.13. 
• The inspector becomes aware that the PIC has not notified the Regulatory Authority 
that an employee is jaundiced or diagnosed with an illness due to a pathogen as 
specified under Sub-¶¶ 2-201.11 (A)(2)(a)-(f) of the Food Code. 
• There are food employees working in the food establishment that have been 
diagnosed with an illness as specified in Sub-¶¶ 2-201.11(A)(2)-(5); Additionally, in 
food establishments exclusively serving a highly susceptible population, there are to 
be no food employees with an active sore throat with a fever working in the food 
establishment. 
N.A. Do Not Mark this item N.A. 
N.O. Do Not Mark this item N.O. 
Applicable Code Sections:  
• 2- 201.11(D) and (F) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person in Charge, and Conditional 
Employees Responsibility of the PIC to Exclude or Restrict (P) 
• 2- 201.12 Exclusions & Restrictions (P) 
• 2- 201.13 Removal, Adjustment, or Retention of Exclusions & Restrictions (P)  
 
5. Illness Documentation. 
IN/OUT This item should be marked IN or OUT of compliance. This item is marked IN compliance 
when it is demonstrated that the food establishment has available for employees a written 
employee health policy addressing symptoms and illness reporting, exclusion/restriction, 
reinstatement, and regulatory reporting requirements in accordance with §§ 2- 201.11, 2-
201.12, and 2-201.13; and written procedures for responding to vomiting or diarrheal 
events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food 
establishment in accordance with § 2-502.11.  
 
This item is marked OUT of compliance if the required written employee health policy 
and/or vomiting or diarrheal events procedures are not available or do not address Food 
Code requirements.. 
N.A. Do Not Mark this item N.A. 
N.O. Do Not Mark this item N.O. 
Applicable Code Sections:  
• 2- 501.11: Employee Illness Policy Documentation (Pf) 
• 2- 502.11: Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events (Pf)

FDA Food Code 2026 Annex 3. Public Health Reasons/Administrative 
Guidelines 
287 
establishment to develop and maintain a written food employee illness policy specific to 
the needs of their food establishment (See Chapter 2, Subpart 2-501). Regulatory 
officials can benefit by using the information provided below as a basis for determining 
compliance with Subpart 2-201 during a facility food safety inspection. The development 
and effective implementation of an employee illness policy based on the provisions in 
Subpart 2-201 will help to prevent foodborne illness associated with contamination of 
food by ill or infected food employees. The person in charge and food employees 
should be familiar with and able to provide the following information through direct 
dialogue or other means when interviewed by facility managers or regulatory officials. 
Compliance must be based, however, on firsthand observations or information and 
cannot be based solely on responses from the person in charge to questions regarding 
hypothetical situations or knowledge of the Food Code. Also, when designing and 
implementing an employee illness policy, the following information should be considered 
and addressed: 
1. Does the establishment have an employee illness or health policy? If so, are the 
food employees aware of the policy, and is it available in written format and readily 
available for food employees? (Note: A written Employee Illness policy is a new 
requirement in the 2026 Food Code for all food establishments under ¶ 2-501.11).  
2. Does the establishment require conditional employees and food employees to report 
symptoms of diarrhea, vomiting, sore throat with fever, and infected wounds or cuts?  
3. Does the establishment require conditional employees and food employees to report 
certain illnesses, including diagnosis with norovirus, hepatitis A virus, non-typhoidal 
salmonellosis, typhoid fever, shigellosis, or STEC E. coli? 
4. Does the establishment require conditional employees and food employees to report 
exposure to listed illnesses, either through exposure to immediate family members 
diagnosed with a listed illness, or through exposure to a foodborne illness outbreak?  
5. Are the reporting requirements explained to all employees?  
6. What are the reporting requirements for conditional employees, food employees, 
and the food establishment manager?  
7. Are conditional employees asked if they are experiencing certain symptoms or 
illnesses upon offer of employment? If so, which symptoms or illnesses?  
8. If a food employee reports a diagnosis with one of the 6 listed pathogens in the Food 
Code, what questions are asked of the food employee? (The first question every 
food manager should ask a food employee who reports diagnosis with a listed 
pathogen is if the employee is currently having any symptoms.)  
9. Who does the establishment notify when a food employee reports a diagnosis with 
one of the listed pathogens?  
10. Does the establishment require the person in charge or permit holder to notify the 
regulatory authority when a food employee or manager reports a diagnosis with a 
listed pathogen?  
11. What gastrointestinal symptoms would require exclusion of a food employee from 
the food establishment?
